reason: The hypothesis relies on a protective native oxide film and its thermal breakdown, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses Cr₂O₃ passivation in HEAs and Mn-based redox buffering in molten salts, neither of which addresses the behavior of a thin iron oxide film on Q235 steel or its spallation under thermal stress. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Native iron oxide film on Q235 provides room-temperature protection
High-temperature salt exposure causes oxide cracking and spallation
Differential thermal expansion drives oxide breakdown
Oxide breakdown exposes metal and accelerates corrosion
Cr₂O₃ passivation films confer corrosion resistance in HEAs
